source.title: Active Learning in the Overparameterized and Interpolating Regime

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to be the full paper. Some equations and figure graphics are garbled or flattened, but the relevant MNIST text is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses minimum-norm interpolating models and their implicit-regularization rationale to build an active-learning method, but does not test the claim versions about generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports natural-label train and test error for active-learning sample-selection methods on MNIST, but none of the claim versions covers active learning or compares the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, explicit-regularization, model-size, sharpness, or memorized-example conditions. Figure 8 provides no recoverable numerical values in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study uses minimum-norm interpolation and its generalization rationale to develop active learning. Its results concern label selection, decision-boundary discovery, and classification error versus label budget; none tests the comparisons specified by V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that MaxiMin active learning efficiently discovers decision boundaries and clusters, with guarantees in specified settings and experiments showing reduced label requirements. They also identify computational cost as a bottleneck and leave broader neural-network evaluation for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops an active-learning sample-selection method using minimum-norm interpolation; it does not compare the claim versions' generalization interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different sampling behavior for function-norm and data-based-norm criteria; scoreD samples more uniformly across MNIST digit clusters in the described experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 8 compares MNIST binary-classification error against label budget for scoreH, scoreD, and random selection. Section 5.4.1 describes faster error decay for scoreD; numerical test-error differences cannot be recovered from the supplied figure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Active selection with minimum-norm interpolators can improve label efficiency, with data-based selection exploiting cluster structure.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Information Theory
record.problems: For the relevant MNIST test-error comparison, Figure 8 is not numerically recoverable from the supplied text, and no uncertainty estimates are stated.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows: synthetic-data error curves and cluster-selection counts concern active-learning behavior but do not test any listed claim version; the numerical MNIST error values are figure-only.

untested.parts: No paired random-label and natural-label training and held-out evaluation using the same neural-network architecture and recipe.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the width required for interpolation.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted training recipes.
No dropout intervention or comparison involving removal of dropout and weight decay.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization gaps.
No identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: The unreadable curves do not prevent determining that the study tests none of V1–V8. Its weight-norm selection scores do not measure V7's perturbation-based sharpness, and selecting informative examples does not measure V8's memorization-based removal effect.
